That hunk is still in `src/search.py`, next to some extra logging you only needed for testing. Nothing has been pushed yet, and Maeve is about to pull your branch for a demo.
amend-medium-hunk-into-last-search.starting_point: You are on `main`. The latest commit is “Rank exact matches first”. `src/search.py` holds the missing ranking hunk and a logging hunk.
amend-medium-hunk-into-last-search.real_world_context: An unpublished commit that misses part of its own change can be completed by amending it. Staging just that hunk keeps the testing noise out.
amend-medium-hunk-into-last-search.task: Add __only__ the missing ranking hunk from `src/search.py` to the latest commit, keeping its message `Rank exact matches first`. **Leave the logging hunk uncommitted** and finish on `main`.
objective_checks: The latest commit is still named “Rank exact matches first” and now includes the ranking change.
No extra commit was created (the amended commit replaced the old one).
The logging hunk is not committed and is still in src/search.py.
amend-medium-hunk-into-last-search.expected_result: “Rank exact matches first” now includes the ranking change and replaced the old commit. The logging hunk stays in `src/search.py`.
accepted_alternatives: `git add --patch src/search.py`; `git commit --amend --no-edit`; `--message` forms; option order swapped. The message must match exactly.

not_accepted: A new commit for the ranking change, or `git add src/search.py` (whole file), which would include the logging.

HEAD changes include the ranking hunk and not the logging hunk; the logging hunk is still unstaged.

amend-hard-fix-message-then-commit-api.label: Reword, then document the rate limiter
amend-hard-fix-message-then-commit-api.story:
You committed the new rate limiter late last night with the message “stuff”. This morning you also wrote `docs/limits.md` to explain it.

Raven reads history before every release, and wants two clear commits: the limiter under a real name, then the docs in their own commit. Nothing has been pushed.
amend-hard-fix-message-then-commit-api.starting_point: You are on `main`. The latest commit, “stuff”, adds `src/limiter.py`. `docs/limits.md` is a new, uncommitted file.
amend-hard-fix-message-then-commit-api.real_world_context: Amend rewrites the most recent commit, so order matters. Rename the commit before adding another one, or the amend would rewrite the wrong commit.
amend-hard-fix-message-then-commit-api.task: Rename the latest commit to `Add rate limiter`, then commit `docs/limits.md` separately with the message `Document rate limits`. Finish on `main`.
objective_checks: The limiter commit is now named “Add rate limiter” and does not contain the docs.
“Document rate limits” comes right after it, with docs/limits.md.
Nothing is left uncommitted, and you finish on main.
amend-hard-fix-message-then-commit-api.expected_result: `main` reads “Add rate limiter” followed by “Document rate limits”, each with its own files.
accepted_alternatives: `--message` forms, single quotes, option order swapped. The messages must match exactly.
Common patterns that apply: P7, P1.
not_accepted: Committing the docs first and amending afterwards (that renames the docs commit), or amending the docs into the limiter commit.
evaluation: `main` has 3 commits; the last amend replaced `c2`; `main~1` = `Add rate limiter` with `src/limiter.py` and without `docs/limits.md`.
`main` = `Document rate limits` adding `docs/limits.md`; clean tree.

restore-easy-discard-theme.label: Throw away the neon theme

restore-easy-discard-theme.task: Discard your edits to `styles/theme.css` and restore its committed version. Finish on `main`.

evaluation: Latest commit on `main` = `Fix login redirect`; changes include `src/login.py`, not `notes/todo.md`.

restore-hard-capstone-report.label: Clean up before the report fix
